identity.name: Kingdom of Gaochang
native_names: 麴氏王國 (Qushi Wangguo, the Qu kingdom)

land.text: Gaochang, where the Northern Liang remnants led by Juqu Wuhui and Juqu Anzhou 'fled to Gaochang' in 439 and ruled until 460

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Northern Liang row ends 440; the page ends the Juqu regime at Gaochang in 460 when the Rouran conquered it.

land.text: Gaochang, 'annexed by the Chinese Tang dynasty and turned into a sub-prefecture of Xizhou' on 19 September 640

successors.note: Xi Prefecture became the seat of the Anxi Protectorate on 11 October 640.

capitals.name: Gaochang (Karakhoja)
capitals.note: 'an ancient oasis city on the northern rim of the inhospitable Taklamakan Desert'; the Tang renamed the prefecture Xi in 640.

correction.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis and its depression

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The page gives no area and no extent beyond 'an ancient oasis city' and its sub-prefecture status in 640; Hou Junji 'annexed Gaochang territory except for three cities' (Hou Junji page). The Turfan oasis (41,000 km2 by a 120 km radius) is the reading: Hami (Yiwu) is not tied to the kingdom by any page opened (the Gaoche page does not link the Fufuluo to Hami either), and the 479 Hephthalite and Gaoche overlordships left the king in place.

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis and its depression

ledger.note: 460: the Rouran install Kan Bozhou as king of Gaochang. 'In 439, remnants of the Northern Liang ... fled to Gaochang ... until 460 when they were conquered by the Rouran Khaganate'; the Rouran 'appointed a Han Chinese named Kan Bozhou to rule as King of Gaochang in 460'.

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis, Kan Bozhou's kingdom

ledger.note: 460: the Gaochang kings rule as Rouran vassals. The Rouran 'appointed a Han Chinese named Kan Bozhou to rule as King of Gaochang in 460'; 'it became a separate vassal kingdom of the Khaganate' and 'Kan was dependent on Rouran backing' (Gaochang page). Mirrors the rouran-khaganate dossier's 460 vassal_start (confidence 3, Rouran page), which draws the oasis 80 km round Gaochang; 120 km here is this dossier's own radius.

481: the Fufuluo (Gaoche) break the Rouran hold. 'In 481, the Fufuluo began to interfere with the Gaochang and deposed one of their kings' (Gaoche page); the page adds 'The Fufuluo were then subjugated by the Rouran Khaganate', and the Gaochang page has Qu Jia (501-525) 'at first pledged allegiance to the Rouran', neither dated, so no second Rouran vassalage is drawn. Mirrors the rouran-khaganate dossier's 481 vassal_end. The year is the Gaoche page's; that the king deposed was the Rouran client is the researcher's reading.

c. 488: the Kan family gives way to the Zhang. The Gaoche king killed Kan Shougui ('478-488?' or '478-491?') and 'Gaochang thus passed under Gaoche rule'; Zhang Mengming '488?-496' follows. Year uncertain by the page itself.

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis under Zhang Mengming

ledger.note: c. 488: Gaochang passes under Gaoche rule. The Gaoche king A-Fuzhiluo 'killed King Kan Shougui, who was the nephew of Kan Bozhou', 'appointed a Han from Dunhuang, named Zhang Mengming' and 'Gaochang thus passed under Gaoche rule' (Gaochang page); the reign table dates Kan Shougui '478-488? or 478-491?' and Zhang Mengming '488?-496 or 491?-496', so the year is the page's with its query mark. The Gaoche page's earlier 'In 481, the Fufuluo began to interfere with the Gaochang' leaves 481-488 without a recorded overlord.
496: the Ma family succeeds the Zhang. Ma Ru '496-501' in the page's reign table.
501: the Qu dynasty begins. 'Qushi Kingdom (501-640 CE)'; Qu Jia '501-525'. The Qu rule to the Tang conquest.

541: the Fufuluo statelet ends. 'They escaped and established a state northwest of Gaochang in 487' and 'the Fufuluo suffered a series of defeats from Anagui before being annihilated in 541' (Gaoche page). The 541 year is the page's for the Fufuluo; that Gaochang's dependence ended with it is the researcher's reading, since the Gaochang page gives no end to the Gaoche overlordship. The Gaoche page's separate 605-612 episode (a Tiele revolt took Gaochang, which 'still remained as their vassal until 612') is not drawn.

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis, the Qu kingdom

ledger.note: 587: the Qu kingdom as a Turkic vassal (bridge). 'The Qu dynasty of Gaochang became vassals of the Göktürks' (Gaochang page), with no year; 587 is the start year of the western-gokturks dossier's ledger 1 (Cliopatria's, not a page's). That dossier names this state by the string 'Kingdom of Gaochang (Qu family)'. Hou Junji page: 'Around the new year of 640, Qu Wentai ... formed an alliance with Western Tujues', an alliance, not drawn as a tie.

19 September 640: the Turkic tie ends with the Tang conquest. 'On 19 September 640 Hou Junji of Tang conquered Gaochang' (Protectorate page); the Western Turks, Qu Wentai's allies, did not intervene on the pages opened. Mirrors western-gokturks ledger 16 (640, 'Gaochang falls').

region.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis and its depression

ledger.note: 19 September 640: Hou Junji conquers Gaochang. 'On 19 September 640 Hou Junji of Tang conquered Gaochang and set up Xi Prefecture in its place'; Xi became the seat of the Anxi Protectorate on 11 October. Hou Junji page: Qu Wentai, allied with the Western Tujue, 'died of distress' and his son Qu Zhisheng surrendered; Taizong 'annexed Gaochang territory except for three cities'.

wars.name: Gaoche interference in Gaochang

wars.outcome: 'In 481, the Fufuluo began to interfere with the Gaochang and deposed one of their kings'; the Gaoche king A-Fuzhiluo killed Kan Shougui and Gaochang passed under Gaoche rule.
wars.note: The Gaochang page gives Kan Shougui's reign as 478-488? or 478-491?.

wars.name: Tang conquest of Gaochang

zones.text: the Gaochang (Turfan) oasis and its depression

wars.outcome: Taizong sent Hou Junji and Xue Wanjun around the new year of 640; Qu Wentai died, Qu Zhisheng surrendered, Xi Prefecture was set up on 19 September 640.
wars.note: The Western Turks, Qu Wentai's allies, did not intervene on the pages opened.

certainty.note: An oasis kingdom: the pages give a city and its depression, never a frontier; the 640 annexation excepted 'three cities'.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks Gaochang; the Qocho Kingdom row is the later Uyghur state, 843-1370). Revised after review (ia-01-x fix pass). The Rouran dossier (ia-01-c) uses the slug 'kingdom-of-gaochang' for its 460 vassal_start and 481 vassal_end; both now have a mirror here (ledger 1 and 2). The Gaoche overlordship is now drawn: vassal_start c. 488 and vassal_end 541, counterpart string 'Gaoche (Fufuluo)' (no Gaoche dossier exists). The Western Turkic vassalage is drawn at confidence 1 (587-640): the Gaochang page says the Qu 'became vassals of the Göktürks' without a year and western-gokturks ledger 1 and 16 carry 587 and 640 under the string 'Kingdom of Gaochang (Qu family)', which should become the slug kingdom-of-gaochang; Hou Junji page dates only the alliance, 'Around the new year of 640'. Left out: the Hephthalite 479 claim over Turfan (White Huns dossier; it appears on neither the Gaochang nor the Gaoche page), the Tiele revolt of 605-612 (Gaoche page: Gaochang 'still remained as their vassal until 612'), and Qu Jia's undated first allegiance to the Rouran. Month: this dossier ends on 19 September 640 (Protectorate page, Xi Prefecture); the Tang example dossier dates the gain to October (11 October, the Anxi Protectorate), a month apart. No area, no capital change: the capital stayed at Gaochang. Rulers are not given: the page's reign table is read only to 501-525 and 623-640. The 640 end is 19 September (Protectorate page); Hou Junji page says the campaign began 'around the new year of 640'. Kingdom of Gaochang also needs a gap-filler for Hami/Yiwu if a page ties it to the kingdom. Gazetteer names used (Gaochang place) resolve.
